title: Misleading Average Rate Calculation (Arithmetic Mean of Rates)
pattern: Using the arithmetic mean to calculate the average rate of a metric (like throughput or transfer rate) across data segments of varying sizes.
why_bad: The arithmetic mean of rates is mathematically incorrect when the duration or volume of work at each rate differs. To find the true average rate of a set of intervals, you must use the harmonic mean (the count of values divided by the sum of their reciprocals). For example, sending 100 MB at 50 MB/s and 700 MB at a throttled rate of 10 MB/s yields a true rate of 11.1 MB/s, whereas an arithmetic average of rates suggests a false 30 MB/s.
detection: Look for arithmetic averages computed directly over rate units (e.g., `MB/s`, `ops/sec`) without weighting by time or volume.
counterexample: Valid only if the volume (or distance) is identical for all rate measurements, making the arithmetic mean acceptable.
strength: Strong` — mathematically incorrect unless the denominator of each rate is identical.
